issues.legal_issue: A law listed in the protected schedule cannot be challenged for violating the protected right to property merely by relying on the corresponding property protection under the former constitutional regime.
material_facts: The challenged law abolished the relevant land tenures, vested specified property in the government, extinguished the former holders’ rights, and provided for compensation.
The law was specifically listed in the protected schedule after a constitutional amendment.
The appellants argued that the compensation was illusory and challenged the law under the former constitutional property protection; the law had not received a separate presidential certificate.
The appeals arose from proceedings challenging the law’s validity, and the court did not decide the adequacy of compensation on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The law’s validity could not be challenged on the asserted property-right ground, including by relying on the corresponding protection under the former constitutional regime; the appeals were dismissed with costs.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-B protects laws listed in the Ninth Schedule from being treated as void on the ground that they are inconsistent with, or take away or abridge, rights protected by Part III. The property-acquisition protection at issue was in substance a fundamental right, although it had previously been secured as a restraint on legislative power by section 299 of the Government of India Act, 1935. The form in which that earlier protection was expressed does not permit a challenge that Article 31-B otherwise bars. The court distinguished The State of Bihar v. Maharajadhiraja Sir Kameshwar Singh of Darbhanga (1952 SCR 889), which concerned legislative competence and an alleged fraud on legislative power rather than the property-right challenge presented here.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A person brings a proceeding challenging the validity of a law.
predicates.challenged_law_is_listed_in_protected_sc: The challenged law is specifically included in a schedule that protects listed laws from specified rights-based challenges.
predicates.challenge_concerns_protected_property_ri: The challenger claims that the law violates a protected right governing the acquisition or deprivation of property.

issues.definition: When a validity challenge concerns a law in the protected schedule and rests on the protected property right, the challenge is barred.
